title: Proposal: stop triggering navigations to about:blank on iframe insertion
body:
(This was discussed a bit in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6491#issuecomment-801155357 but I'm making a separate issue since it's quite orthogonal, and since I just thought about a potential way forward on this)

**Background**
When an iframe is created/inserted it will [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#the-iframe-element:navigate-an-iframe-or-frame-2) to the URL from its `src` attribute (if it's set and the `srcdoc` attribute is unset), replacing the initial empty document. If this URL is `about:blank`, in the current spec, it should still replace the initial empty document with a new `about:blank` document. I think this navigation is triggered in all browsers, but how it runs (synchronously/asynchronously) and its effect (removing the "initial about:blank document"-ness or not) differs (see next section). Also, when the `src` attribute is not set, according to the spec the iframe should stay on the initial empty document. However, at least in Chrome this actually triggers an `about:blank` navigation, as if the `src` is set to `about:blank`.

**Behavior of the `about:blank` navigation on initial insertion**
* In Chrome and probably Safari, the navigation happens synchronously when the iframe is inserted. This means the initial empty document is immediately replaced by the non-initial about:blank. However, in both Chrome and Safari, the non-initial about:blank is actually treated the same way as the initial empty document. So, the end result is pretty much the same with not navigating at all (see https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/28541)
* In Firefox, the navigation happens asynchronously - this means the initial empty document will be available for a while until it got replaced by the new `about:blank` document. Since it's asynchronous, the navigation can be canceled (e.g. by document.open(), as mentioned in this [comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6491#issuecomment-801155357)). After the navigation finished, the iframe will not show the initial empty document anymore.

**Web-exposed behavior differences**
1. The "initial empty document"-ness differs across browsers as mentioned above. In Chrome & Safari, the new `about:blank` document will still be considered as the initial empty document, while in Firefox it's not. This has an impact on whether future navigations will replace that document or not. For more details see https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/28541 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6491.

2. The document will be replaced asynchronously in Firefox, while it's replaced synchronously/immediately in Chrome and Safari. I think this is actually a very big difference, because in Chrome & Safari you can do this and the text will stay, while in Firefox it will be cleared when the new document committed:
 ```js
  let f = document.createElement("iframe");
  frameContainer.appendChild(f);
  f.contentDocument.body.innerHTML = "some text";
  ```
Tester pages to compare in various browsers: [iframe with no src](https://rakina.github.io/inject-nosrc.html), [iframe with src="about:blank"](https://rakina.github.io/inject-src-aboutblank.html)

**Proposal: stop triggering navigations to about:blank on iframe insertion**
I propose that we stop triggering navigations to `about:blank` on iframe insertion, so that when an iframe with `src` set to `about:blank` is inserted, it will just stay on the initial empty document, similar to when `src` is not set (at least the spec version). My reasoning is as follows:
* This is essentially what is already happening (probably unintentionally) in Chrome and Safari since both the "initial empty document"-ness and the document will be kept after the iframe is inserted.
* Although the document is actually the new `about:blank` document committed synchronously, it's virtually indistinguishable from the initial empty document: the origin and other document properties should be the same, and it's not possible to get a reference to the initial empty document before insertion so nobody knows that it was ever there to begin with.
* This is the same behavior as `window.open()` when the URL is not set, empty or is `about:blank`: instead of triggering a navigation, it will just [fire](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/window-object.html#apis-for-creating-and-navigating-browsing-contexts-by-name:event-load) the `load` event on the window (see [test page](https://rakina.github.io/inject-window-open.html)).

Potential problems:
* Firefox behavior will need to change to follow Chrome and Safari here. I think this is reasonable, especially the part where we stop changing the document asynchronously after potentially modifying it. I don't think Chrome and Safari can follow Firefox's behavior here without potentially breaking some websites that depend on being able to modify the iframe's document immediately after creation.
* Events/side effects from navigations. I think since in Chrome and Safari the navigation was already synchronous to begin with, it's not possible to observe events/changes related to navigations on the document/window. For example, we can't add a `load` event listener to the `contentWindow` before insertion, and the `load` event would've already fired if we try to add it after insertion. I'm not sure if this has any effect on the `load` event on the `<iframe>` itself, but I think we can just fire the `load` event here too like the `window.open()` case above. CMIIW! 
* Keeping the "initial empty document" status means the next same-origin document will reuse the `Window` (see https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3267). I think this is already what's happening in Chrome and maybe Safari, I haven't checked though. Not really sure if this is bad, but since browsers already have support for this maybe it's not really a big deal?
* [Maybe there are some subtleties I'm missing, please let me know if so!]

cc @domenic @annevk @zetafunction @ArthurSonzogni @csreis who might be interested.

PS: I think some Chrome folks were thinking of [following](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KY0DCaoKjUPbOX28N9KWvBjbnAfQEIRTaLbZUq9EkK8/edit#heading=h.7zppq4c0qp4a) Firefox's behavior previously to remove all cross-document synchronous commits in Chrome's renderer, but I recently found some tests in Chrome that do not expect the document to be changed asynchronously, and pretty worried that this exists in real websites, so I think it's probably best to just avoid this special navigation entirely, and it's pretty consistent with the `window.open()` case too!
